messages:
maya: Hey team, just got a ticket from AcmeCorp — their SSO-provisioned API key can call embeddings fine but generation endpoints 403. Customer says they never asked for an embeddings-only key. Can someone help triage? Org: org-acme-1123, key masked: sk-***-acme.
ben:  Adding context from support: they tried both /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions and both returned 403 with 'missing scope: generation'. Embeddings (/v1/embeddings) succeeded. They also tried rerank endpoint and got 403 'missing scope: rerank'.
maya: Repro steps I ran quickly (local):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***-acme" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"hello"}'
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient_scope",
    "message": "missing scope: generation"
  }
}
```
Embeddings curl succeeded with 200 and vectors returned.
ryan: Thanks. Two quick questions: (1) was this key created via SSO JIT provisioning or via our Admin UI? (2) Do we know whether the org has any legacy provisioning templates? :eyes:
ben: Customer says the key was created from their IdP SSO button (so JIT). They mentioned they used our old SSO integration months ago and never rotated keys.
olivia: I pulled the provisioning audit for org-acme-1123. The provisioner logged a template id 'tpl-emb-v1' at creation time.
Provisioner log lines (sanitized):
```
2026-03-12T09:12:13Z PROVISION create_key org=org-acme-1123 user=alice@acme.com template=tpl-emb-v1 key_id=sk-xxxx
2026-03-12T09:12:13Z PROVISION resolved_scopes ["embeddings"]
```
So looks like the JIT flow selected an embeddings-only template.
maya: Any idea why the JIT flow would pick that template? Customer insists they expected full inference scopes.
olivia: Two possible reasons:
1) Org metadata still had a deprecated flag `default_scopes: embeddings_only` set from an old onboarding flow. Our provisioner is supposed to merge org defaults with IdP requested scopes, but there's a bug where if an org default exists we take it exclusively. (that's the bug I'm looking at)
2) A template mapping for their IdP group might have been misconfigured.
ryan: Can you dump the resolved scope payload the provisioner used? If it's only ["embeddings"] that's our smoking gun.
olivia: Here's the resolved payload for that create_key call:
```
{"org_id":"org-acme-1123","requested_scopes":[],"org_defaults":["embeddings"],"resolved_scopes":["embeddings"]}
```
Note requested_scopes is empty because IdP didn't supply scope hints in the SAML assertion (we don't require that). The bug is the merge step.
maya: Ok that explains the 403s. What are the mitigation options for the customer now? They need generation + rerank in prod.
olivia: Short-term workarounds:
- Admin UI: have an org admin exchange the key for a new key and explicitly select generation+rerank scopes (fastest).
- Admin API (internal): we can call internal POST /internal/admin/keys/patch-scopes to add scopes to the existing key.
- Reprovision: force a new JIT with correct template after we patch org metadata.
ryan: For the admin API, post an example we can run for support to apply (will need elevated creds):
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/internal/admin/keys/patch-scopes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer internal-svc-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"key_id":"sk-xxxx","add_scopes":["generation","rerank"]}'
```
Response will be 200 and key metadata updated.
ben: I can ask the customer if they want us to perform the admin patch. They prefer us to do it rather than rotate their app secrets today.
maya: Please also surface the incident to eng-platform — this is a logic bug that will cause accidental embeddings-only keys for other orgs that have legacy defaults.
olivia: I've created ENG-TICKET-5891 and assigned to platform; summary: "Provisioner merge bug defaults to org_defaults single-scope template ignoring requested scopes for SSO JIT." I also included the audit snippet. Proposed fix: change merge to union(requested_scopes, org_defaults) and add a warning if requested_scopes is empty.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: patch to provisioner library to change merge behavior will be deployed to staging in ~30m. CI job: provisioning-e2e
ryan: Once patch is in staging, let's run an e2e repro: create a test org with org_defaults=["embeddings"] and trigger SSO JIT with no requested scopes — we should get union -> embeddings + generation (generation via fallback template) instead of only embeddings.
olivia: Agreed. I'll also add a migration job that finds keys provisioned in last 12 months where resolved_scopes == ["embeddings"] and org_defaults contains other scopes; flag them for mitigation.
maya: For the immediate customer outreach: Ben, please offer (1) a temporary admin patch by support, (2) or they can rotate via UI, (3) ETA for engineering fix ~ 6 hours to staging + smoke tests, prod deploy after +1 day. Also include apology and explanation.
ben: On it. I'll update ticket and ask for consent to patch key. Customer responded: "please patch it, we can't rotate right now" and provided org admin approval.
maya: I applied the admin patch for sk-xxxx, verified generation and rerank calls now return 200. Example response snippet from /v1/generate now:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"id":"gen_abc123","output":"Hello from Redwood"}
```
Customer confirmed in support portal that their app is green. :thumbsup:
olivia: I'll keep ENG-TICKET-5891 open until we have the deploy and the migration job run. After deploy we'll backfill affected keys and notify orgs.
maya: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: (1) ben to confirm customer notification, (2) olivia to post postmortem note in #eng-platform when done, (3) ryan to add an alert if a key is created with resolved_scopes being a strict subset of org_defaults (sanity check).
ben: All set — customer notified and happy. Closing support escalation after postmortem.
